name: Agentic Finance Graph — answers to the manifesto research questions
note: Both questions were published in the manifesto with our expectation. The rules were written down before either query ran; both results are published as they fell. Drafted with AI assistance; every figure is from the queries in this folder.

q1.question: Of all USDC that left agent-bound wallets on Base since 3 February 2026, how much does the spending share move when each exclusion rule is removed on its own?
q1.expectation: The pre-registration rule moves it most.
q1.answer: The routing-hop rule moves the spending share most (+36.6 points by value), not the pre-registration rule (+6.7). Most pre-registration money (123.7M of 156.8M USD) was also a routing hop, so removing the pre-registration rule alone leaves it excluded. Our expectation was wrong.

reconciles_to_published.note: the same SQL without the USDC and date filters reproduces both published metrics to the cent (snapshots of 2026-10-23 08:27 and 06:59 UTC)

q2.question: Does the volume of on-chain reputation feedback predict whether an agent later pays anyone, once the ten most active raters are set aside?

preregistered_robustness.result: not computable: binding records begin 2026-09-06, so no agent had a binding valid at this T0

q2.answer: Feedback volume does not predict later paying in a usable way. On the pre-registered cohort it came out worse than chance: agents with more feedback were less likely to start paying (0.60% with none, 0.07% with five or more). A cohort one week later, added after we saw that and not pre-registered, sits within chance and leans the other way. Our expectation (no better than chance) was wrong on the pre-registered test, on the low side.
does_not_assert: That feedback causes or prevents paying.
That any rater is fake or any agent bad.
